chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, all together from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Zurara who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) was in the Sacred Masjid, so he mentioned the Clan of Umayya and their government. Some of his companions said to him, 'We hope that you will become their master and that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will Display this Command upon your hands.' So he said, 'I am not their master, nor am I happy to be their master, for their companions are the sons of adultery. Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, never Created, since the creation of the Heavens and the earth, years nor days shorter than their years and their days. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, Orders the Angel who holds the orbit in his hand to rotate it like a scroll.'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Abu Ja'far say about the Banu Umayya and their governance?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (AS) responds to companions' hopes for his political dominance by rejecting the Umayyad lineage, famously labeling their companions as 'sons of adultery' to highlight their illegitimacy. He illustrates the brevity of their rule by citing a divine decree where the Angel of the Sphere is commanded to rotate the heavens rapidly, symbolizing how swiftly their days and years passed compared to the eternal duration of the Ahl al-Bayt's legacy.
